anatomy.intro: Four structures that explain the form of the probable compact Espostoa.

parts.function: Fine pale hairs screen the green surface beneath.
parts.label: Woolly covering

parts.function: A sharp projecting spine remains hidden among the soft-looking hairs.
parts.label: Central spine

parts.function: The spine-bearing cushion organizes the wool and spines along the stem.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: The living stem stores water and photosynthesizes beneath its covering.
parts.label: Green ribbed stem

flowers.text: RHS describes Espostoa flowers at genus level as white and bell- or cup-shaped, opening at night. This is a mature-plant feature; a small woolly nursery cactus should not be expected to flower on a schedule.

growth.note: The illustration shows the probable identity; growth alone will not settle the subspecies.

stages.text: A short woolly column establishes its ribbed body.
stages.title: Compact juvenile

stages.text: Fresh tissue and new wool appear at the growing tip.
stages.title: Taller stem

stages.text: The parent species can form a clump of upright columns.
stages.title: Older branching plant

habitat.text: Kew records Espostoa melanostele subsp. nana from Ancash, Peru, in desert and dry shrubland. That is the background of the working identification, not a known collection locality for this nursery plant. Its woolly upright body fits Espostoa, but the precise identification remains probable, with E. lanata also considered.

lookalikes.name: Golden ball cactus
lookalikes.text: Parodia leninghausii has golden bristles rather than the thick white wool characteristic of this plant.

mature.text: The parent species is columnar and clump-forming, with 20–30 ribs. Its published size should not be treated as a precise ceiling for this uncertain compact plant.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch individual pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

nameStory.text: Kew recognizes nana as a subspecies under a combination published in 2002; it was first described as Espostoa nana in 1964.
